ramayana-7-8-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-7.translation: 'I must always do what is dear to the gods, even at the cost of my life. So I will defeat you, even if you go to the underworld.'
ramayana-7-8-7.meaning: He would protect the gods wherever the rakshasas went.
ramayana-7-8-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself. Teaching: a protector keeps his promise to those who depend on him.

ramayana-7-8-8.translation: As the red-lotus-eyed god said this, the rakshasa lord, enraged, struck him with a spear and roared.
ramayana-7-8-8.meaning: Malyavan hurled a spear at Vishnu.
ramayana-7-8-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-8-9.translation: The spear released from Malyavan's arm, ringing with bells, shone on Hari's chest like lightning in a cloud.
ramayana-7-8-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-10.translation: Then the lotus-eyed one, dear to the spear-bearer Skanda, pulled out that very spear and hurled it at Malyavan.
ramayana-7-8-10.meaning: Vishnu pulled out the spear and threw it back.
ramayana-7-8-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-11.translation: Released from Govinda's hand, as if thrown by Skanda, the spear sped towards the rakshasa like a great meteor at the Anjana mountain.
ramayana-7-8-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-12.translation: It fell on the rakshasa lord's broad chest, bright with his necklace, like a thunderbolt on a mountain peak.
ramayana-7-8-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-8-13.translation: With his armour pierced by it, Malyavan sank into deep darkness; but he recovered and stood firm as a mountain.
ramayana-7-8-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-14.translation: Then he took a black iron spike covered with many thorns and struck the god hard in the middle of the chest.
ramayana-7-8-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-8-15.translation: And the night-roamer, loving battle, struck Indra's younger brother with his fist and then drew back a bow's length.
ramayana-7-8-15.meaning: He punched Vishnu and stepped back.
ramayana-7-8-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-16.translation: Then a great cry of 'Well done! Well done!' rose in the sky. Having struck Vishnu, the rakshasa also struck Garuda.
ramayana-7-8-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-17.translation: Then Vinata's son, enraged, swept the rakshasa away with the wind of his wings, as a strong wind sweeps away a heap of dry leaves.
ramayana-7-8-17.meaning: Garuda blew Malyavan away like dry leaves.
ramayana-7-8-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-18.translation: Seeing his elder brother driven off by the wind of the king of birds' wings, Sumali went with his forces towards Lanka.
ramayana-7-8-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-19.translation: Malyavan too, blown away by the force of the wings' wind, rejoined his forces and went to Lanka, covered with shame.
ramayana-7-8-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-20.translation: 'So, lotus-eyed Rama, those rakshasas were broken many times in battle by Hari, and their foremost leaders were slain.'
ramayana-7-8-20.meaning: Vishnu defeated them again and again.
ramayana-7-8-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-8-21.translation: 'Unable to fight Vishnu and troubled by fear, they left Lanka and went with their wives to live in the underworld.'
ramayana-7-8-21.meaning: They abandoned Lanka and went underground.
ramayana-7-8-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-22.translation: 'Gathering around the rakshasa Sumali, joy of the Raghus, those of famed valour lived in the line of Salakatankata.'
ramayana-7-8-22.meaning: They lived on in the underworld with Sumali.
ramayana-7-8-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-23.translation: 'Those you defeated were rakshasas called Paulastyas. Sumali, Malyavan, Mali and those who led them were all stronger than Ravana, fortunate one.'
ramayana-7-8-23.meaning: Agastya explained that these earlier rakshasas were stronger than Ravana.
ramayana-7-8-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-8-24.translation: 'And no one else, even among the gods, could slay rakshasas, conqueror of cities, except the god Narayana, who bears the conch, discus and mace.'
ramayana-7-8-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

keywords.meaning: bearer of conch, discus and mace

ramayana-7-8-25.translation: 'You are the god Narayana, four-armed and eternal, born to slay the rakshasas, unconquerable, the imperishable lord.'
ramayana-7-8-25.meaning: Agastya reminded Rama that he is Narayana himself.
ramayana-7-8-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 8: Malyavan challenges Vishnu and is driven off; the rakshasas leave Lanka for the underworld. Agastya tells Rama he is Narayana himself.

ramayana-7-9-1.translation: 'After some time, the rakshasa named Sumali came up from the underworld and wandered through the whole world of mortals.'
ramayana-7-9-1.meaning: Years later, Sumali came up from the underworld.
ramayana-7-9-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-2.translation: 'Dark as a blue cloud, wearing earrings of burnished gold, he took his young daughter, like Shri without her lotus, and saw the lord of wealth going by in the Pushpaka.'
ramayana-7-9-2.meaning: With his daughter, Sumali saw Kubera flying in the Pushpaka.
ramayana-7-9-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-3.translation: 'Seeing him go by, like an immortal, bright as fire, the rakshasa said to his daughter, whose name was Kaikasi:'
ramayana-7-9-3.meaning: He spoke to his daughter Kaikasi.
ramayana-7-9-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-4.translation: '"Daughter, it is time for you to be married; your youth is passing. Because of you, all of us who care about dharma are held back."'
ramayana-7-9-4.meaning: Sumali told her it was time to marry.
ramayana-7-9-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-5.translation: '"You have every good quality, little daughter, like Shri with her lotus. Suitors, afraid of being refused, do not ask for you."'
ramayana-7-9-5.meaning: Suitors were too shy to ask for her.
ramayana-7-9-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-6.translation: '"Being a girl's father is hard for all who care for honour, daughter, for one does not know who will ask for her."'
ramayana-7-9-6.meaning: Fathers worry about who will marry their daughters.
ramayana-7-9-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-7.translation: '"A girl always keeps three families in suspense: her mother's family, her father's family, and the one she is given to."'
ramayana-7-9-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-8.translation: '"So, daughter, go yourself to Vishravas, son of Pulastya, best of sages, born of Prajapati's line, and choose him."'
ramayana-7-9-8.meaning: Sumali asked her to go to the sage Vishravas.
ramayana-7-9-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-9.translation: '"Your sons will surely be like this lord of wealth, daughter, equal to the sun in radiance."'
ramayana-7-9-9.meaning: He hoped her sons would be as powerful as Kubera.
ramayana-7-9-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth. Sumali's ambition for power sets the stage for Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-10.translation: 'At that time, Rama, Pulastya's son, the brahmin, was tending his sacred fire, like a fourth fire.'
ramayana-7-9-10.meaning: Vishravas was performing his evening fire ritual.
ramayana-7-9-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-11.translation: 'Out of respect for her father, she did not think about that harsh hour, but went up to him and stood before him, her face lowered to his feet.'
ramayana-7-9-11.meaning: Obeying her father, Kaikasi went to Vishravas at an unlucky hour and stood shyly before him.
ramayana-7-9-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Sumali sees Kubera's glory and sends his daughter Kaikasi to the sage Vishravas; this is the beginning of Ravana's birth.

ramayana-7-9-12.translation: 'Seeing her, with fine hips and a face like the full moon, the most generous sage, glowing with power, spoke.'
ramayana-7-9-12.meaning: Vishravas saw Kaikasi and spoke to her.
ramayana-7-9-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-13.translation: '"Good lady, whose daughter are you? Where have you come from? What is your purpose, and for whose sake? Tell me truly, lovely one."'
ramayana-7-9-13.meaning: He asked who she was and why she had come.
ramayana-7-9-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-14.translation: 'So addressed, the girl said with joined palms: "Sage, by your own power you can know my mind."'
ramayana-7-9-14.meaning: She replied that he could know her purpose through his wisdom.
ramayana-7-9-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-15.translation: '"But know, brahmin, that I have come at my father's command. My name is Kaikasi; the rest you can know yourself."'
ramayana-7-9-15.meaning: She said her father had sent her and her name was Kaikasi.
ramayana-7-9-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-16.translation: 'The sage went into meditation and said: "I know, good lady, the purpose that is in your mind."'
ramayana-7-9-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-17.translation: '"Because you have come to me at a harsh hour, hear, good lady, what kind of sons you will bear."'
ramayana-7-9-17.meaning: Because she came at an unlucky hour, he foretold her sons' nature.
ramayana-7-9-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-18.translation: '"You will give birth to fierce rakshasas, of fierce form, fond of fierce company, and cruel in deeds."'
ramayana-7-9-18.meaning: Her sons would be fierce and cruel.
ramayana-7-9-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-19.translation: 'Hearing this, she bowed and said: "Lord, such sons are not fitting to come from you, born of Brahma's line."'
ramayana-7-9-19.meaning: She pleaded that his sons should be good.
ramayana-7-9-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-20.translation: 'Then the sage said: "Your last son will be worthy of my line and righteous."'
ramayana-7-9-20.meaning: The sage promised that her youngest son would be righteous.
ramayana-7-9-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera. This foretells Vibhishana.

ramayana-7-9-21.translation: 'Told this, Rama, the girl after some time gave birth to a terrifying child in rakshasa form.'
ramayana-7-9-21.meaning: In time, Kaikasi gave birth to a fearsome son.
ramayana-7-9-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-22.translation: 'He had ten heads and great fangs, dark as a heap of collyrium, with copper-coloured lips, twenty arms, a huge mouth and blazing hair.'
ramayana-7-9-22.meaning: He had ten heads and twenty arms.
ramayana-7-9-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-23.translation: 'As soon as he was born, jackals with flaming mouths and flesh-eating creatures circled to the left.'
ramayana-7-9-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera. Omens like these warn of coming disaster in the epic.

ramayana-7-9-24.translation: 'The sky rained blood, clouds roared harshly, the sun did not shine in the sky, and great meteors fell to earth.'
ramayana-7-9-24.meaning: The skies showed signs of doom.
ramayana-7-9-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera. Omens like these warn of coming disaster in the epic.

ramayana-7-9-25.translation: 'Then his father, equal to the Grandsire, named him: "Born with ten heads, he will be Dashagriva."'
ramayana-7-9-25.meaning: He was named Dashagriva, 'ten-necked', later known as Ravana.
ramayana-7-9-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-26.translation: 'After him was born mighty Kumbhakarna, whose size is unmatched by anything here.'
ramayana-7-9-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-27.translation: 'Then was born Shurpanakha, of misshapen face, and righteous Vibhishana, Kaikasi's last son.'
ramayana-7-9-27.meaning: Then Shurpanakha, and last the good Vibhishana.
ramayana-7-9-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-28.translation: 'They grew up in that great forest, very powerful. Of them, cruel Dashagriva became a troubler of the worlds.'
ramayana-7-9-28.meaning: Ravana grew up cruel and troubled the world.
ramayana-7-9-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-29.translation: 'Wicked Kumbhakarna, heedless, roamed about frightening the three worlds and harming the great sages devoted to dharma.'
ramayana-7-9-29.meaning: Kumbhakarna harmed sages and frightened everyone.
ramayana-7-9-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-30.translation: 'But righteous Vibhishana always kept to the path of dharma, living with study, measured food and controlled senses.'
ramayana-7-9-30.meaning: Vibhishana lived a disciplined, righteous life.
ramayana-7-9-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera. Teaching: one's nature is chosen by conduct, not by family.

ramayana-7-9-31.translation: 'Then after some time the lord of wealth came in the Pushpaka to see his very powerful father.'
ramayana-7-9-31.meaning: Kubera came to visit their father.
ramayana-7-9-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-32.translation: 'Seeing him there, blazing with splendour, Kaikasi, with a rakshasa's mind, said to Dashagriva:'
ramayana-7-9-32.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-33.translation: '"Son, look at your brother Vaishravana, surrounded by splendour. Though you are equally his brother, see how you are."'
ramayana-7-9-33.meaning: She compared Ravana unfavourably with his brother Kubera.
ramayana-7-9-33.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera. Teaching: envy and comparison can plant the seeds of great harm.

ramayana-7-9-34.translation: '"Dashagriva, of boundless valour, make such an effort that you soon become like Vaishravana, my son."'
ramayana-7-9-34.meaning: She urged him to become as great as Kubera.
ramayana-7-9-34.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-35.translation: 'Hearing his mother's words, mighty Dashagriva was filled with great resentment and made a vow.'
ramayana-7-9-35.meaning: Ravana became resentful and made a vow.
ramayana-7-9-35.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-36.translation: '"I truly promise you, mother, I will soon be equal to my brother or even greater. Give up the sorrow in your heart."'
ramayana-7-9-36.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-9-37.translation: 'Then, in that same anger, Dashagriva with his younger brothers resolved, "I will gain my wish through austerity," and went to the holy hermitage of Gokarna to win success.'
ramayana-7-9-37.meaning: The brothers went to Gokarna to perform austerities.
ramayana-7-9-37.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 9: Kaikasi bears Vishravas four children: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Shurpanakha and the righteous Vibhishana; Ravana vows to match Kubera.

ramayana-7-10-1.translation: Then Rama said to the brahmin: 'How did those brothers practise austerity in the forest, brahmin, and what were their great vows like?'
ramayana-7-10-1.meaning: Rama asked how they did their austerities.
ramayana-7-10-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-2.translation: Agastya told Rama, who listened attentively, of the various disciplines of dharma those brothers took up there.
ramayana-7-10-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-3.translation: 'Kumbhakarna, focused and devoted to dharma, practised austerity in summer standing among five fires.'
ramayana-7-10-3.meaning: Kumbhakarna sat among five fires in summer.
ramayana-7-10-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-4.translation: 'In the rains, soaked by the clouds' water, he kept the hero's posture, and in winter he always stayed in the middle of water.'
ramayana-7-10-4.meaning: He endured rain and cold water too.
ramayana-7-10-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-5.translation: 'Thus ten thousand years passed for him, striving in dharma and established on the good path.'
ramayana-7-10-5.meaning: He kept this up for a very long time.
ramayana-7-10-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-6.translation: 'Righteous Vibhishana, always devoted to dharma and pure, stood on one foot for five thousand years.'
ramayana-7-10-6.meaning: Vibhishana stood on one foot for ages.
ramayana-7-10-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-7.translation: 'When his vow was complete, the apsaras danced, a shower of flowers fell, and the gods were stirred.'
ramayana-7-10-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-8.translation: 'For five thousand years he followed the sun, standing with head and arms raised, his mind fixed on study.'
ramayana-7-10-8.meaning: He worshipped the sun with arms raised.
ramayana-7-10-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-9.translation: 'So ten thousand years passed for self-controlled Vibhishana too, as if he were in heaven in the Nandana garden.'
ramayana-7-10-9.meaning: For Vibhishana, these years passed happily.
ramayana-7-10-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-10.translation: 'Ten-faced Ravana fasted for ten thousand years, and at the end of each thousand years he offered one of his heads into the fire.'
ramayana-7-10-10.meaning: Ravana fasted and offered one of his heads to the fire every thousand years.
ramayana-7-10-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep. The extreme imagery shows the fierce, self-willed nature of Ravana's austerity.

ramayana-7-10-11.translation: 'Thus nine thousand years passed, and nine of his heads had entered the fire.'
ramayana-7-10-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-12.translation: 'Then in the ten-thousandth year, as he was about to cut off his tenth head, the Grandsire arrived.'
ramayana-7-10-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-13.translation: 'The Grandsire, very pleased, came with the gods and said, "Child, child Dashagriva, I am pleased."'
ramayana-7-10-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-14.translation: '"Quickly choose the boon you desire, knower of dharma. What wish shall I grant you today? Your effort shall not be in vain."'
ramayana-7-10-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-15.translation: 'Then Dashagriva, glad at heart, bowed his head to the god and spoke in a voice choked with joy.'
ramayana-7-10-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-16.translation: '"Lord, living beings always fear nothing so much as death. There is no enemy like death, so I choose immortality."'
ramayana-7-10-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-17.translation: '"Lord of creatures, let me be forever unslayable by Garudas, nagas, yakshas, daityas, danavas, rakshasas and gods."'
ramayana-7-10-17.meaning: He asked to be unbeatable by all heavenly and demonic beings.
ramayana-7-10-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-18.translation: '"I do not care about other creatures, you who are worshipped by the immortals. To me all living beings, men and the rest, are like straw."'
ramayana-7-10-18.meaning: He did not bother to ask protection from humans, whom he thought worthless.
ramayana-7-10-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep. Teaching: Ravana's contempt for humans becomes his undoing, for Vishnu is born as a man.

ramayana-7-10-19.translation: 'Thus addressed by the rakshasa Dashagriva, the righteous Grandsire with the gods spoke, Rama.'
ramayana-7-10-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-20.translation: '"So it shall be for you, bull among rakshasas. Hear also my further kind words, since I am pleased."'
ramayana-7-10-20.meaning: Brahma granted it and added more.
ramayana-7-10-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-21.translation: '"The heads you offered earlier into the fire, sinless one, shall be yours again as before, rakshasa."'
ramayana-7-10-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-22.translation: 'At the Grandsire's words, the heads of the rakshasa Dashagriva that had been offered into the fire rose up again.'
ramayana-7-10-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-23.translation: 'Having said this to Dashagriva, Rama, Prajapati, Grandsire of the world, spoke to Vibhishana.'
ramayana-7-10-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-24.translation: '"Vibhishana, child, I am pleased with you, whose mind is joined with dharma. Choose a boon, knower of dharma, you of good vows."'
ramayana-7-10-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-25.translation: 'Righteous Vibhishana, always full of every virtue like the moon with its rays, spoke with joined palms.'
ramayana-7-10-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-26.translation: '"Lord, I am fulfilled, since the teacher of the worlds himself is pleased with me. If you must give me a boon, hear it, you of good vows."'
ramayana-7-10-26.meaning: Vibhishana said Brahma's pleasure was already enough.
ramayana-7-10-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-27.translation: '"Whatever thoughts arise in me, in whatever situation of life, may they always be most righteous, and may I uphold that dharma."'
ramayana-7-10-27.meaning: He asked that his mind always choose what is right.
ramayana-7-10-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep. Teaching: Vibhishana's wish is not for power but for a mind that always chooses rightly.

ramayana-7-10-28.translation: '"This, most generous one, I think is the highest boon. For those devoted to dharma, nothing in the world is hard to gain."'
ramayana-7-10-28.meaning: For those who live rightly, nothing is out of reach.
ramayana-7-10-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-29.translation: 'Then Prajapati, pleased, said to Vibhishana: "As you are most righteous, child, so it shall be."'
ramayana-7-10-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-30.translation: '"Because, though born among rakshasas, your mind does not turn to adharma, I also give you immortality, tamer of foes."'
ramayana-7-10-30.meaning: Brahma also gave him long life for staying good despite his birth.
ramayana-7-10-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-31.translation: 'As Prajapati was about to give a boon to Kumbhakarna, all the gods said to him with joined palms:'
ramayana-7-10-31.meaning: The gods stopped Brahma before he blessed Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-7-10-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-32.translation: '"Do not give a boon to Kumbhakarna yet, for you know how this evil-minded one terrifies the worlds."'
ramayana-7-10-32.meaning: They warned that Kumbhakarna was dangerous.
ramayana-7-10-32.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-33.translation: '"In Nandana he has harmed seven apsaras and ten followers of great Indra, brahmin, and sages and humans too."'
ramayana-7-10-33.meaning: They listed the harm he had done.
ramayana-7-10-33.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-34.translation: '"Under the guise of a boon, let him be given delusion, you of boundless splendour. Then the worlds will be safe, and he will be humbled."'
ramayana-7-10-34.meaning: They asked that his boon be turned into a confusion.
ramayana-7-10-34.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-35.translation: 'Thus addressed by the gods, lotus-born Brahma thought, and at his thought the goddess Sarasvati came to his side.'
ramayana-7-10-35.meaning: Brahma called upon Sarasvati, goddess of speech.
ramayana-7-10-35.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-36.translation: 'Standing at his side with joined palms, Sarasvati said: "Here I am, god. What task shall I do?"'
ramayana-7-10-36.meaning: Sarasvati asked what she should do.
ramayana-7-10-36.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-37.translation: 'Prajapati said to Sarasvati: "Speech, be in the rakshasa lord's mouth as the gods wish."'
ramayana-7-10-37.meaning: Brahma asked her to guide Kumbhakarna's words.
ramayana-7-10-37.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-38.translation: 'She agreed and entered him. Then Prajapati said: "Kumbhakarna, mighty-armed one, choose the boon you want."'
ramayana-7-10-38.meaning: Brahma asked Kumbhakarna for his wish.
ramayana-7-10-38.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-39.translation: 'Hearing this, Kumbhakarna said: "God of gods, I wish to sleep for many years."'
ramayana-7-10-39.meaning: Kumbhakarna asked to sleep for many years.
ramayana-7-10-39.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep. The goddess of speech turned his words, so his boon became sleep.

ramayana-7-10-40.translation: 'Saying "So be it" to him, the Grandsire with the gods, and the goddess Sarasvati, leaving him, went to heaven.'
ramayana-7-10-40.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-10-41.translation: 'Then wicked Kumbhakarna, troubled, thought: "What kind of words are these that have fallen from my mouth today?"'
ramayana-7-10-41.meaning: Kumbhakarna was shocked at what he had said.
ramayana-7-10-41.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep. Teaching: careless words can shape one's whole life.

ramayana-7-10-42.translation: 'Having thus received their boons, all the brothers, blazing with energy, went to the Shleshmataka forest and lived there happily.'
ramayana-7-10-42.meaning: The brothers lived happily after their boons.
ramayana-7-10-42.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 10: The three brothers perform great austerities; Brahma grants Ravana near-invulnerability, Vibhishana a mind always set on dharma, and Kumbhakarna long sleep.

ramayana-7-11-1.translation: 'Learning that those night-roamers had received boons, Sumali gave up his fear and rose from the underworld with his followers.'
ramayana-7-11-1.meaning: Hearing of the boons, Sumali came up from the underworld.
ramayana-7-11-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-2.translation: 'Maricha, Prahasta, Virupaksha and Mahodara, the rakshasa's ministers, rose up full of eagerness.'
ramayana-7-11-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-3.translation: 'Surrounded by all these chief rakshasas, Sumali went to Dashagriva, embraced him, and said:'
ramayana-7-11-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-4.translation: '"By good fortune, son, this long-held wish of ours is fulfilled, since you have received such a boon from the best of the three worlds."'
ramayana-7-11-4.meaning: Sumali was thrilled with Ravana's boon.
ramayana-7-11-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-5.translation: '"The great fear of Vishnu, for which we left Lanka and went to the underworld, is gone, mighty-armed one."'
ramayana-7-11-5.meaning: Now they need not fear Vishnu.
ramayana-7-11-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-6.translation: '"Defeated by him again and again, we left our own home and fled together to the underworld."'
ramayana-7-11-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-7.translation: '"This city of Lanka, where rakshasas lived, is ours; your wise brother, the lord of wealth, has settled it."'
ramayana-7-11-7.meaning: Lanka was ours, but now Kubera lives there.
ramayana-7-11-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-8.translation: '"If it is possible to win it back by persuasion, by gifts, or by force, mighty-armed one, that would be done."'
ramayana-7-11-8.meaning: Get it back by any means.
ramayana-7-11-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-9.translation: '"And you, dear one, will be lord of Lanka without doubt, and the master of us all, mighty one."'
ramayana-7-11-9.meaning: You will be king of Lanka.
ramayana-7-11-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-10.translation: 'Then Dashagriva said to his grandfather: "The lord of wealth is our elder; you should not speak like this."'
ramayana-7-11-10.meaning: At first Ravana refused, saying Kubera is his elder brother.
ramayana-7-11-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-11.translation: 'As Dashagriva said this, the night-roamer Prahasta spoke respectful words with reasons.'
ramayana-7-11-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-12.translation: '"Mighty-armed Dashagriva, you should not say this. There is no brotherly love among heroes. Hear my words."'
ramayana-7-11-12.meaning: Prahasta said that heroes do not let brotherhood hold them back.
ramayana-7-11-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way. This is bad counsel; the epic shows the harm it brings.

ramayana-7-11-13.translation: '"Aditi and Diti, two very beautiful sisters, were wives of Prajapati Kashyapa."'
ramayana-7-11-13.meaning: He told a story about Aditi and Diti.
ramayana-7-11-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-14.translation: '"Aditi bore the gods, lords of the three worlds, and Diti bore the daityas, both sons of Kashyapa."'
ramayana-7-11-14.meaning: Their sons became the gods and the daityas.
ramayana-7-11-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-15.translation: '"This earth, with its forests, oceans and mountains, once belonged to the daityas, hero; they were powerful."'
ramayana-7-11-15.meaning: The earth once belonged to the daityas.
ramayana-7-11-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-16.translation: '"But Vishnu slew them in battle, and the imperishable three worlds came under the gods' control."'
ramayana-7-11-16.meaning: Then the gods took it from them.
ramayana-7-11-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-17.translation: '"You will not be the only one to do such a reversal. The gods did it before. Follow my advice."'
ramayana-7-11-17.meaning: Even the gods took from their brothers, so you may too.
ramayana-7-11-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-18.translation: 'Thus addressed by wicked Prahasta, Dashagriva thought for a moment and said, "Very well."'
ramayana-7-11-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-19.translation: 'In that same joy, mighty Dashagriva went that very day to the forest with those night-roamers.'
ramayana-7-11-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-20.translation: 'Standing on Trikuta, the night-roamer Dashagriva sent Prahasta, skilled in speech, as his messenger.'
ramayana-7-11-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-21.translation: '"Prahasta, go quickly and tell the lord of wealth, chief of the nairritas, these words of mine, gently at first:"'
ramayana-7-11-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-22.translation: '"King, this city of Lanka belongs to the great rakshasas. You have settled it, gentle one, and that is not right of you, sinless one."'
ramayana-7-11-22.meaning: He claimed Lanka belonged to the rakshasas.
ramayana-7-11-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-23.translation: '"So if you give it up peacefully, you of matchless valour, I will be pleased and dharma will be upheld."'
ramayana-7-11-23.meaning: He asked Kubera to give it up peacefully.
ramayana-7-11-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-24.translation: 'So told, Prahasta, skilled in speech, went and told the lord of wealth all of Dashagriva's words.'
ramayana-7-11-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-25.translation: 'Hearing these words from Prahasta, the god Vaishravana, skilled in speech, replied to Prahasta.'
ramayana-7-11-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-26.translation: '"Go and tell Dashagriva: this city and kingdom that are mine are yours too, mighty-armed one. Enjoy it, free of trouble."'
ramayana-7-11-26.meaning: Kubera generously offered to share Lanka.
ramayana-7-11-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way. Teaching: Kubera answers greed with generosity.

ramayana-7-11-27.translation: '"I will do all you say soon, lord of rakshasas, bless you. But wait until I tell our father."'
ramayana-7-11-27.meaning: He asked to consult their father first.
ramayana-7-11-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-28.translation: 'Having said this, the lord of wealth went to his father, saluted him and told him what Ravana wanted.'
ramayana-7-11-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-29.translation: '"Father, Dashagriva has sent me a messenger: 'Give up the city of Lanka, where rakshasas once lived.' Tell me what I should do, you of good vows."'
ramayana-7-11-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-30.translation: 'Thus addressed, the brahmin sage Vishravas, chief of sages, said to the giver of wealth: "Listen to my words, son."'
ramayana-7-11-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-31.translation: '"Mighty-armed Dashagriva said this in my presence. I scolded him and told the wicked one many things."'
ramayana-7-11-31.meaning: Their father had already scolded Ravana.
ramayana-7-11-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-32.translation: '"In anger I told him again and again, 'You will be ruined.' Now hear my words, son, which are good and righteous."'
ramayana-7-11-32.meaning: He warned Ravana he would be ruined, and now advised Kubera.
ramayana-7-11-32.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: Sumali urges Ravana to take Lanka; Ravana demands it from Kubera, and their father Vishravas advises Kubera to give way.

ramayana-7-11-33.translation: '"Confused by his boon, the very wicked one does not know whom to respect and whom not, and because of my curse he has taken on a cruel nature."'
ramayana-7-11-33.meaning: Ravana's boon had made him arrogant and cruel.
ramayana-7-11-33.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-11-34.translation: '"So go, mighty-armed one, to Mount Kailasa that holds up the earth. Settle there to live, and leave Lanka with your followers."'
ramayana-7-11-34.meaning: Vishravas advised Kubera to move to Kailasa.
ramayana-7-11-34.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-11-35.translation: '"There flows the lovely Mandakini, best of rivers, its waters covered with golden lotuses bright as the sun."'
ramayana-7-11-35.meaning: Kailasa is beautiful, with the lovely Mandakini river.
ramayana-7-11-35.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-11-36.translation: '"It is not wise for you to make an enemy of that rakshasa, giver of wealth, for you know what a great boon he has won."'
ramayana-7-11-36.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka. Teaching: sometimes stepping back is wiser than fighting.

ramayana-7-11-37.translation: 'So told, he accepted those words out of respect for his father and left with his wives, citizens, ministers, mounts and wealth.'
ramayana-7-11-37.meaning: Kubera obeyed his father and left Lanka.
ramayana-7-11-37.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka. Teaching: Kubera gives up his city rather than fight his brother.

ramayana-7-11-38.translation: 'Prahasta went to Dashagriva and told him everything: "The city of Lanka, thirty leagues long, is empty. Enter it with us and uphold your own dharma there."'
ramayana-7-11-38.meaning: Prahasta told Ravana that Lanka was now empty.
ramayana-7-11-38.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-11-39.translation: 'So told by Prahasta, the rakshasa Ravana then entered the city of Lanka with his brothers, army and followers.'
ramayana-7-11-39.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-11-40.translation: 'Consecrated by the night-roamers, ten-faced Ravana settled the city, and it became full of night-roamers like dark clouds.'
ramayana-7-11-40.meaning: Ravana was crowned king of Lanka.
ramayana-7-11-40.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-11-41.translation: 'The lord of wealth, respecting his father's word, built a city on the moon-pure mountain, adorned with well-decorated mansions, like Indra's Amaravati.'
ramayana-7-11-41.meaning: Kubera built a new city on Kailasa.
ramayana-7-11-41.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 11: On his father's advice Kubera leaves Lanka for Mount Kailasa, and Ravana is crowned king of Lanka.

ramayana-7-12-1.translation: 'When the rakshasa lord had been crowned along with his brothers, he thought about giving his rakshasi sister in marriage.'
ramayana-7-12-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-2.translation: 'He gave his sister, the rakshasi named Shurpanakha, to Vidyujjihva, lord of the Kalakeya danavas.'
ramayana-7-12-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-3.translation: 'Having given his sister away, the king went roaming on a hunt, and there, Rama, he saw Maya, son of Diti.'
ramayana-7-12-3.meaning: While hunting, Ravana met Maya, the architect of the asuras.
ramayana-7-12-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-4.translation: 'Seeing him with a young girl, the night-roamer Dashagriva asked: "Who are you, alone in this forest without people, full of deer?"'
ramayana-7-12-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-5.translation: 'Maya, Rama, told the night-roamer who asked: "Listen, I will tell you all that has happened to me."'
ramayana-7-12-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-6.translation: '"Dear one, you may have heard of the apsara named Hema. The gods gave her to me, as Pauloma's daughter was given to Indra."'
ramayana-7-12-6.meaning: The gods gave Maya the apsara Hema as wife.
ramayana-7-12-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-7.translation: '"My heart was attached to her for five hundred years, but she has been gone for fourteen years on the gods' business."'
ramayana-7-12-7.meaning: She had left on the gods' work.
ramayana-7-12-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-8.translation: '"For Hema's sake I created by my magic a whole golden city, bright with diamonds and lapis."'
ramayana-7-12-8.meaning: Maya had built a golden city for her.
ramayana-7-12-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-9.translation: '"Finding no joy there without her and very unhappy, I took my daughter from that city and came to the forest."'
ramayana-7-12-9.meaning: Lonely without her, he came to the forest.
ramayana-7-12-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-10.translation: '"This is my daughter, king, raised in Hema's womb. I have come with her to seek a husband for her."'
ramayana-7-12-10.meaning: He was looking for a husband for his daughter.
ramayana-7-12-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-11.translation: '"Being a girl's father is hard for men who care for honour, for a girl always keeps two families in suspense."'
ramayana-7-12-11.meaning: A daughter's marriage concerns two families.
ramayana-7-12-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-12.translation: '"Two sons were born to me by this wife: Mayavi first, dear one, and then Dundubhi."'
ramayana-7-12-12.meaning: Maya's sons were Mayavi and Dundubhi.
ramayana-7-12-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born. These are the same Mayavi and Dundubhi whom Vali later fought.

ramayana-7-12-13.translation: '"I have told you all this truly since you asked. Now, dear one, how may I know who you are?"'
ramayana-7-12-13.meaning: Maya asked Ravana who he was.
ramayana-7-12-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-14.translation: 'Thus addressed, the rakshasa lord said politely: "I am the son of Pulastya's son, and my name is Dashagriva."'
ramayana-7-12-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-15.translation: 'Knowing him to be the son of a brahmin sage, Maya was delighted and decided to give him his daughter.'
ramayana-7-12-15.meaning: Maya chose Ravana as his son-in-law.
ramayana-7-12-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-16.translation: 'Smiling, the daitya lord said to the rakshasa lord: "King, this is my daughter, born of the apsara Hema. Her name is Mandodari; accept her as your wife."'
ramayana-7-12-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-17.translation: 'Dashagriva said, "Very well," Rama, and lighting a fire there he took her hand in marriage.'
ramayana-7-12-17.meaning: Ravana married Mandodari by the sacred fire.
ramayana-7-12-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-18.translation: 'Maya did not know of the curse from the ascetic, Rama; he gave her knowing only of his grandfather's family.'
ramayana-7-12-18.meaning: Maya did not know of the sage's warning about Ravana.
ramayana-7-12-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-19.translation: 'He also gave him a most wonderful, unfailing spear, won by great austerity, with which Lakshmana was struck.'
ramayana-7-12-19.meaning: Maya gave Ravana the spear that later wounded Lakshmana.
ramayana-7-12-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-20.translation: 'Married thus, the lord of Lanka went to the city and arranged wives for his two brothers.'
ramayana-7-12-20.meaning: Ravana found wives for his brothers.
ramayana-7-12-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-21.translation: 'Ravana arranged for Kumbhakarna to marry Vajrajvala, granddaughter of Virochana.'
ramayana-7-12-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-22.translation: 'Righteous Vibhishana won as his wife Sarama, daughter of the great gandharva king Shailusha.'
ramayana-7-12-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born. Sarama later comforts Sita in Lanka.

ramayana-7-12-23.translation: 'She was born on the shore of Lake Manasa, and the lake, dear one, rose with the coming of the rains.'
ramayana-7-12-23.meaning: Sarama was born by Lake Manasa as it was flooding.
ramayana-7-12-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-24.translation: 'Her mother cried out in love, "Lake, do not rise!" (saro ma vardhata), and so she became Sarama.'
ramayana-7-12-24.meaning: Her name came from her mother's cry to the lake.
ramayana-7-12-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-25.translation: 'So married, those rakshasas enjoyed life there, each with his own wife, like gandharvas in Nandana.'
ramayana-7-12-25.meaning: The brothers lived happily with their wives.
ramayana-7-12-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-26.translation: 'Then Mandodari gave birth to a son, Meghanada, the one you call Indrajit.'
ramayana-7-12-26.meaning: Mandodari had a son, Meghanada, later called Indrajit.
ramayana-7-12-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-27.translation: 'As soon as he was born, that son of the rakshasa cried out with a huge sound like a thunder-cloud.'
ramayana-7-12-27.meaning: As a baby, he cried like thunder.
ramayana-7-12-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-28.translation: 'Lanka was stunned by that sound, so his father himself named him Meghanada, "Thunder".'
ramayana-7-12-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-12-29.translation: 'He grew up, Rama, in Ravana's lovely inner palace, guarded by fine women, like a fire hidden in wood.'
ramayana-7-12-29.meaning: He grew up in Ravana's palace.
ramayana-7-12-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 12: The brothers marry: Ravana weds Mandodari, daughter of Maya, Kumbhakarna weds Vajrajvala, Vibhishana weds Sarama; Indrajit (Meghanada) is born.

ramayana-7-13-1.translation: 'Then after some time, the deep Sleep sent by the lord of the worlds came to Kumbhakarna in bodily form.'
ramayana-7-13-1.meaning: Brahma's boon of sleep came upon Kumbhakarna.
ramayana-7-13-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-2.translation: 'Then Kumbhakarna said to his brother as he sat: "Sleep is overpowering me, king. Have a home built for me."'
ramayana-7-13-2.meaning: Kumbhakarna asked for a house to sleep in.
ramayana-7-13-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-3.translation: 'At the king's order, craftsmen like Vishvakarma built Kumbhakarna a home like Kailasa.'
ramayana-7-13-3.meaning: Builders made him a huge home.
ramayana-7-13-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-4.translation: 'They made for Kumbhakarna a bright home a league wide and twice as long, beautiful and undisturbed.'
ramayana-7-13-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-5.translation: 'It was adorned everywhere with pillars of crystal and gold, beautified with lapis and hung with nets of bells,'
ramayana-7-13-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-6.translation: 'with ivory arches and platforms of diamond and crystal, pleasant in every season, like a holy cave of Meru.'
ramayana-7-13-6.meaning: It was comfortable in every season.
ramayana-7-13-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-7.translation: 'There the night-roamer Kumbhakarna, overcome by sleep, lay for many thousands of years without waking.'
ramayana-7-13-7.meaning: Kumbhakarna slept for thousands of years.
ramayana-7-13-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-8.translation: 'While Kumbhakarna was overcome by sleep, ten-faced Ravana constantly troubled the gods, sages, yakshas and gandharvas.'
ramayana-7-13-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-9.translation: 'Going in great anger to Nandana and the other lovely gardens, ten-faced Ravana destroyed them.'
ramayana-7-13-9.meaning: He wrecked the gardens of heaven.
ramayana-7-13-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-10.translation: 'Like an elephant playing in a river, like the wind tossing trees, like a hurled thunderbolt hitting mountains, he kept on destroying.'
ramayana-7-13-10.meaning: He destroyed everything like a storm.
ramayana-7-13-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-11.translation: 'Learning how Dashagriva behaved, the lord of wealth, knowing dharma and remembering what was fitting for their family and his own conduct,'
ramayana-7-13-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-12.translation: 'Vaishravana, to show brotherly love, sent a messenger to Lanka for Dashagriva's own good.'
ramayana-7-13-12.meaning: Out of brotherly love, Kubera sent a messenger to warn him.
ramayana-7-13-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him. Teaching: Kubera still cares for his brother and tries to guide him.

ramayana-7-13-13.translation: 'Going to the city of Lanka, he met Vibhishana, who honoured him properly and asked why he had come.'
ramayana-7-13-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-14.translation: 'Having asked after the king, his kin and relatives, Vibhishana showed him Dashagriva seated in the assembly.'
ramayana-7-13-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-15.translation: 'Seeing the king there, shining with his own splendour, he honoured him with a wish for victory and stayed silent for a moment.'
ramayana-7-13-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-16.translation: 'Seated on a couch brought for him, covered with fine cloth, the messenger then spoke to Dashagriva.'
ramayana-7-13-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-17.translation: '"King, I will tell you all that your brother said, gentle one, fitting for both your conduct and your family."'
ramayana-7-13-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-18.translation: '"Enough of this; you have done plenty. Now gather good conduct; establish yourself well in dharma, if you can."'
ramayana-7-13-18.meaning: Kubera urged Ravana to stop and turn to dharma.
ramayana-7-13-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-19.translation: '"I have seen Nandana destroyed and heard that sages were slain. I have also heard of the gods' preparations against you, king."'
ramayana-7-13-19.meaning: The gods are preparing to act against you.
ramayana-7-13-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-20.translation: '"You have often slighted me, lord of rakshasas, but even when kinsmen do wrong out of childishness, they must be protected."'
ramayana-7-13-20.meaning: Kubera forgave Ravana's insults as a brother.
ramayana-7-13-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him. Teaching: Kubera's patience with his brother shows true family love.

ramayana-7-13-21.translation: '"I went to the slopes of the Himalaya to practise dharma, taking up a fierce vow, disciplined and with my senses controlled."'
ramayana-7-13-21.meaning: Kubera told of his time in the Himalaya.
ramayana-7-13-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-22.translation: '"There I saw the lord Shiva with the goddess Uma, and my left eye happened to fall upon the goddess,"'
ramayana-7-13-22.meaning: He happened to glance at Parvati.
ramayana-7-13-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-23.translation: '"wondering only, 'Who is this lovely one?', for no other reason; for Parvati was playing there in matchless form."'
ramayana-7-13-23.meaning: He only wondered who she was.
ramayana-7-13-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-24.translation: '"Then by the goddess's power my left eye was burned and turned yellow, like a light dimmed by dust."'
ramayana-7-13-24.meaning: His left eye was scorched and turned yellow.
ramayana-7-13-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-25.translation: '"Then I went to another wide slope of that mountain and kept a great vow for eight hundred years."'
ramayana-7-13-25.meaning: He then kept a long vow.
ramayana-7-13-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-26.translation: '"When the vow was over, the lord Maheshvara, pleased, said these words with a glad heart:"'
ramayana-7-13-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-27.translation: '"'I am pleased with your austerity, knower of dharma, you of good vows. This vow has been kept by me and by you, lord of wealth.'"'
ramayana-7-13-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-28.translation: '"'There is no third person who could keep such a vow. I myself created this very hard vow long ago.'"'
ramayana-7-13-28.meaning: Only Shiva and Kubera had kept this vow.
ramayana-7-13-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-29.translation: '"'So accept friendship with me, lord of wealth. Since you have won it by austerity, be my friend, sinless one.'"'
ramayana-7-13-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-30.translation: '"'And because your left eye was burned by the goddess's power, your name will forever be Ekakshipingala, one-yellow-eye.'"'
