ramayana-7-13-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-31.translation: '"So, having won friendship with Shankara and taken leave of him, I came back and heard of your wicked resolve."'
ramayana-7-13-31.meaning: Kubera, now Shiva's friend, heard of Ravana's misdeeds.
ramayana-7-13-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-32.translation: '"So turn back from associating with the unrighteous, you who disgrace our family. The gods and sages are thinking of a way to end you."'
ramayana-7-13-32.meaning: Turn back from your wrong path; the gods are plotting your end.
ramayana-7-13-32.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-33.translation: 'Thus addressed, Dashagriva, angry with eyes red, clenched his hands and teeth and said:'
ramayana-7-13-33.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-34.translation: '"I understand what you say, messenger. Neither you nor the brother who sent you are anything to me."'
ramayana-7-13-34.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-35.translation: '"This guardian of wealth does not speak for my good. Fool, you tell me of his friendship with Maheshvara as if to frighten me."'
ramayana-7-13-35.meaning: He mocked Kubera's friendship with Shiva.
ramayana-7-13-35.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-36.translation: '"I thought, 'He is my elder brother and not to be harmed.' But now, hearing his words, I have made up my mind."'
ramayana-7-13-36.meaning: Ravana decided to attack his brother.
ramayana-7-13-36.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-13-37.translation: '"Relying on the strength of my arms I will conquer even the three worlds. This very moment, for his sake alone, I will send those four guardians of the world to the abode of Death."'
ramayana-7-13-37.meaning: He boasted that he would defeat all the world guardians.
ramayana-7-13-37.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-13-38.translation: 'Having said this, the lord of Lanka struck down the messenger with his sword.'
ramayana-7-13-38.meaning: In his rage, Ravana killed the messenger.
ramayana-7-13-38.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him. Harming an envoy was one of the gravest wrongs; it shows how far Ravana had fallen.

ramayana-7-13-39.translation: 'Then, after blessings for his journey, Ravana mounted his chariot and, longing to conquer the three worlds, went to where the lord of wealth was.'
ramayana-7-13-39.meaning: Ravana set out to attack Kubera.
ramayana-7-13-39.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 13: Kumbhakarna falls into his long sleep; Ravana troubles the worlds, and when Kubera sends a kind warning, Ravana harms the envoy and marches on him.

ramayana-7-14-1.translation: 'Then, with his six ministers, always fierce in strength, Mahodara and Prahasta, Maricha, Shuka and Sarana,'

ramayana-7-14-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 14: Ravana attacks Kubera's yakshas on Kailasa and fights his way to the city gate.

ramayana-7-14-20.meaning: Maricha recovered and drove the yaksha off.
ramayana-7-14-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 14: Ravana attacks Kubera's yakshas on Kailasa and fights his way to the city gate. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-14-21.translation: 'Then he entered the gateway, the boundary of the gatekeepers, its body bright with gold and set with lapis and silver.'
ramayana-7-14-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 14: Ravana attacks Kubera's yakshas on Kailasa and fights his way to the city gate.

ramayana-7-14-22.translation: 'Then, Rama, a gatekeeper named Suryabhanu stopped the night-roamer Dashagriva as he entered.'
ramayana-7-14-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 14: Ravana attacks Kubera's yakshas on Kailasa and fights his way to the city gate.

ramayana-7-14-23.translation: 'Tearing up the gateway, that yaksha struck the rakshasa with it; but because of the water-born Brahma's boon, Rama, the rakshasa did not fall.'
ramayana-7-14-23.meaning: The gatekeeper struck Ravana with the gate itself, but Brahma's boon protected him.

ramayana-7-14-24.translation: 'He struck the yaksha back with that same gateway, and the yaksha vanished, reduced to ashes.'

ramayana-7-14-25.translation: 'Seeing this valour, all the yakshas fled, and in fear they hid in rivers and caves.'
ramayana-7-14-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 14: Ravana fights his way into Kubera's city and the yakshas flee.

ramayana-7-15-4.translation: 'Then Prahasta struck down a thousand in battle, and Mahodara with his mace another thousand.'
ramayana-7-15-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-15-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-15-10.meaning: Ravana knocked Manibhadra's crown sideways, giving him a new name.
ramayana-7-15-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot.

ramayana-7-15-11.translation: 'When the great yaksha Manibhadra turned away, Rama, a great roar rose on that mountain.'
ramayana-7-15-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot.

ramayana-7-15-12.translation: 'Then from afar the lord of wealth was seen, holding a mace, attended by Shukra and Proshthapada and the treasures Shankha and Padma.'
ramayana-7-15-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot.

ramayana-7-15-13.translation: 'Seeing his brother in battle, fallen from respect because of the curse, the wise one spoke words fitting for their grandfather's family.'
ramayana-7-15-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot.

ramayana-7-15-14.translation: '"Though I tried to stop you, wicked one, you do not understand. Later, when you reap its fruit, you will know it as you go to hell."'
ramayana-7-15-14.meaning: You did not listen; you will learn when you face the results.
ramayana-7-15-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot.

ramayana-7-15-15.translation: '"A man who drinks poison in delusion does not realize it; only at the end does the fool know the fruit of his deed."'
ramayana-7-15-15.meaning: Like drinking poison, the harm of wrong deeds shows itself later.
ramayana-7-15-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Teaching: every action bears its own fruit; this is the law of karma.

ramayana-7-15-16.translation: '"The gods rejoice in anyone joined with dharma. You do not see what has brought you to this state."'
ramayana-7-15-16.meaning: The gods favour the righteous; you do not see how you have fallen.
ramayana-7-15-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot.

ramayana-7-15-17.translation: '"Whoever disrespects mothers, fathers, brothers and teachers sees the fruit of it when he falls under the power of the king of the dead."'
ramayana-7-15-17.meaning: Disrespecting family and teachers brings its own punishment.
ramayana-7-15-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Teaching: honour your parents, siblings and teachers.

ramayana-7-15-18.translation: '"Whoever, in this perishable body, does not earn the merit of austerity, regrets it later, the fool, when he sees his fate after death."'
ramayana-7-15-18.meaning: Use this short life to do good, or regret it later.
ramayana-7-15-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Teaching: life is short; use it to grow in goodness.

ramayana-7-15-19.translation: '"No wicked person gets good sense just by wishing for it. As one acts, so one reaps."'
ramayana-7-15-19.meaning: As you act, so you will reap.
ramayana-7-15-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Teaching: every action bears its own fruit; this is the law of karma.

ramayana-7-15-20.translation: '"Intelligence, beauty, strength, wealth, children and greatness: people gain all of these through their own past deeds."'
ramayana-7-15-20.meaning: What we have comes from what we have done.
ramayana-7-15-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 15: Kubera himself faces Ravana, warns him that every deed bears fruit, but is defeated; Ravana takes the Pushpaka chariot. Teaching: every action bears its own fruit; this is the law of karma.

ramayana-7-15-21.translation: '"You are bound for hell, since your mind is like this. I will not speak with you further; this is my judgement on the wicked."'

ramayana-7-16-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-2.translation: 'Then Dashagriva saw the golden reed forest, surrounded by a web of rays like a second sun.'
ramayana-7-16-2.meaning: He saw the shining golden reeds.
ramayana-7-16-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-3.translation: 'Reaching a mountain with a lovely forest, he saw the Pushpaka stopped in the sky there, Rama.'
ramayana-7-16-3.meaning: Suddenly the Pushpaka stopped in mid-air.
ramayana-7-16-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-4.translation: 'Seeing the Pushpaka, which goes where it wishes, now stuck and unable to move, the rakshasa, surrounded by his ministers, wondered.'
ramayana-7-16-4.meaning: Ravana wondered why it would not move.
ramayana-7-16-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-5.translation: '"What is this? Why does the Pushpaka not go? Whose doing could this be, of someone on this mountain?"'
ramayana-7-16-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-6.translation: 'Then Maricha, wise in counsel, said to Dashagriva: "This is not without reason, king, that the Pushpaka does not move."'
ramayana-7-16-6.meaning: Maricha said there must be a reason.
ramayana-7-16-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-7.translation: 'Then Shiva's mighty attendant Nandishvara came near and fearlessly said to the rakshasa lord:'
ramayana-7-16-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-8.translation: '"Turn back, Dashagriva. Shankara is at play on this mountain."'
ramayana-7-16-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-9.translation: '"This mountain has been made off-limits to all beings: Garudas, nagas, yakshas, daityas, danavas and rakshasas."'
ramayana-7-16-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-10.translation: 'Copper-eyed with anger, he got down from the Pushpaka, said "Who is this Shankara?", and went to the foot of the mountain.'
ramayana-7-16-10.meaning: Ravana angrily went to see who was blocking him.
ramayana-7-16-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-11.translation: 'Then he saw lord Nandishvara standing nearby, holding a blazing trident, like a second Shankara.'
ramayana-7-16-11.meaning: He saw Nandi holding a trident.
ramayana-7-16-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-12.translation: 'Seeing his monkey-like face, the rakshasa scorned him and foolishly burst out laughing, like a rain cloud thundering.'
ramayana-7-16-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-13.translation: 'Angered, lord Nandi, Shankara's second form, spoke to the rakshasa Dashagriva standing there.'
ramayana-7-16-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-14.translation: '"Wicked rakshasa, because you see me in monkey form and foolishly scorn me and laugh,"'
ramayana-7-16-14.meaning: Because you mocked my monkey face,
ramayana-7-16-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-15.translation: '"monkeys of my form, with valour and splendour like mine, will be born to destroy your family."'
ramayana-7-16-15.meaning: monkeys like me will bring about your family's downfall.
ramayana-7-16-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'. This curse foreshadows the monkey army that helps Rama.

ramayana-7-16-16.translation: '"But what can I do to you now, night-roamer? You need not be struck down, for you are already struck down by your own deeds."'
ramayana-7-16-16.meaning: Your own deeds will destroy you.
ramayana-7-16-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'. Teaching: every action bears its own fruit; this is the law of karma.

ramayana-7-16-17.translation: 'Ignoring Nandi's words, the night-roamer went up to the mountain and said:'
ramayana-7-16-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-18.translation: '"Lord of cattle, I will uproot this mountain for whose sake the Pushpaka's course was stopped as I travelled."'
ramayana-7-16-18.meaning: He threatened to uproot the mountain.
ramayana-7-16-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-16-19.translation: '"By what power does Bhava play here like a king? He does not know the danger that has come."'
ramayana-7-16-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-16-20.translation: 'Having said this, king, he thrust his arms under the mountain and lifted it, with its deer, beasts and trees.'
ramayana-7-16-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-21.translation: 'Then, Rama, Mahadeva, smiling as he watched, playfully pressed the mountain down with his big toe.'
ramayana-7-16-21.meaning: Shiva calmly pressed the mountain down with one toe.
ramayana-7-16-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'. Teaching: true power is calm; pride is undone with ease.

ramayana-7-16-22.translation: 'Then his arms, pinned under the mountain, were crushed, and the rakshasa's ministers were amazed.'
ramayana-7-16-22.meaning: Ravana's arms were trapped under the mountain.
ramayana-7-16-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-23.translation: 'From anger and the pain in his arms, the rakshasa let out a huge cry that filled the three worlds.'
ramayana-7-16-23.meaning: Ravana cried out so loudly that the worlds shook.
ramayana-7-16-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-24.translation: 'People, terrified by the sound, thought the world was ending, and even the gods were shaken in their work.'
ramayana-7-16-24.meaning: Everyone was frightened by the cry.
ramayana-7-16-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-25.translation: 'Then Mahadeva, pleased, standing on the mountain top, released his arms and spoke to ten-faced Ravana, king.'
ramayana-7-16-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'. Ravana is said to have praised Shiva in song at this time, which pleased him.

ramayana-7-16-26.translation: '"I am pleased with your valour and your daring, night-roamer. In your pain you let out a most terrible cry."'
ramayana-7-16-26.meaning: Shiva was pleased with his courage.
ramayana-7-16-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-27.translation: '"Because the three worlds were made to cry out and were seized with fear, you shall be known by the name Ravana."'
ramayana-7-16-27.meaning: Shiva named him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.
ramayana-7-16-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-28.translation: '"Gods, men, yakshas and all others on earth will call you Ravana, the one who makes the worlds cry."'
ramayana-7-16-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

keywords.meaning: one who makes the worlds cry

ramayana-7-16-29.translation: '"Go, Paulastya, without fear, by whatever path you wish. I give you leave, lord of rakshasas; go."'
ramayana-7-16-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-30.translation: 'Named thus by Maheshvara himself, Ravana bowed to Mahadeva and climbed into the chariot.'
ramayana-7-16-30.meaning: Ravana bowed to Shiva and left.
ramayana-7-16-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-16-31.translation: 'Then, Rama, Ravana roamed the earth, troubling mighty kshatriyas here and there.'
ramayana-7-16-31.meaning: Ravana went on troubling kings across the earth.
ramayana-7-16-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 16: On Kailasa, Ravana mocks Nandi and tries to lift the mountain; Shiva presses it down with his toe, and names him Ravana, 'the one who made the worlds cry out'.

ramayana-7-17-1.translation: 'Then, king, mighty-armed Ravana, roaming the earth, came to the Himalayan forest and wandered there.'
ramayana-7-17-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-2.translation: 'There he saw a maiden wearing black deerskin and matted hair, following the rules of the sages and practising austerity like a goddess.'
ramayana-7-17-2.meaning: He saw a young woman meditating like a sage.
ramayana-7-17-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-3.translation: 'Seeing that beautiful maiden of great vows, his mind overcome by desire and delusion, he asked her, as if laughing:'
ramayana-7-17-3.meaning: Ravana, overcome with desire, spoke to her.
ramayana-7-17-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-4.translation: '"Why do you live like this, good lady, against your youth? This practice does not suit your beauty."'
ramayana-7-17-4.meaning: He asked why someone so young lived so austerely.
ramayana-7-17-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-5.translation: '"Whose daughter are you, good lady, and who is your husband, sinless one? Tell me quickly, since I ask, why you practise austerity."'
ramayana-7-17-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-6.translation: 'So addressed by that ignoble rakshasa, the maiden rich in austerity, after duly offering him hospitality, said:'
ramayana-7-17-6.meaning: She welcomed him properly and replied.
ramayana-7-17-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita. Teaching: she shows courtesy even to an unworthy guest.

ramayana-7-17-7.translation: '"My father was the righteous brahmin sage named Kushadhvaja, glorious son of Brihaspati, equal to Brihaspati in wisdom."'
ramayana-7-17-7.meaning: Her father was the sage Kushadhvaja.
ramayana-7-17-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-8.translation: '"As that great soul was always studying the Vedas, I was born from it as a maiden made of speech, known by the name Vedavati."'
ramayana-7-17-8.meaning: She was named Vedavati, born of the Vedas.
ramayana-7-17-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-9.translation: '"Then gods with gandharvas, yakshas, rakshasas and nagas went to my father and asked for my hand."'
ramayana-7-17-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-10.translation: '"But my father did not give me to them, lord of rakshasas. I will tell you the reason; listen, mighty-armed one."'
ramayana-7-17-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-11.translation: '"My father wanted Vishnu, best of the gods, lord of the three worlds, as his son-in-law; so my father would not give me to anyone else."'
ramayana-7-17-11.meaning: Her father wished her to marry Vishnu.
ramayana-7-17-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-12.translation: '"Hearing that the righteous one wished this, a daitya king named Shambhu, proud of his strength, grew angry, and that wicked one attacked my father at night as he slept."'
ramayana-7-17-12.meaning: A demon king, angered, attacked her father in his sleep.
ramayana-7-17-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-13.translation: '"Then my grieving mother, that noble lady, embraced my father's body and entered the fire with him."'
ramayana-7-17-13.meaning: Her mother, in grief, followed her father in death.
ramayana-7-17-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-14.translation: '"Then the wish arose firmly in my heart: 'I will make true my father's wish regarding Narayana.'"'
ramayana-7-17-14.meaning: She resolved to fulfil her father's wish.
ramayana-7-17-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-15.translation: '"'I will do what my father wanted even though he is gone.' Making this vow, I practise great austerity."'
ramayana-7-17-15.meaning: She practises austerity to marry Vishnu.
ramayana-7-17-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita. Teaching: Vedavati's devotion to her father's wish and to Vishnu is unwavering.

ramayana-7-17-16.translation: '"I have told you all this, bull among rakshasas. Know that I have taken refuge in dharma, wishing for Narayana as my husband."'
ramayana-7-17-16.meaning: She has given her life to dharma and Vishnu.
ramayana-7-17-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-17.translation: '"I know who you are, king. Go, son of the Paulastya line. By my austerity I know all that happens in the three worlds."'
ramayana-7-17-17.meaning: She knew who he was and asked him to leave.
ramayana-7-17-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-18.translation: 'Then Ravana, getting down from the chariot and struck by desire, spoke to that maiden of great vows.'
ramayana-7-17-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-19.translation: '"You are proud, lovely one, to think like this. Piling up merit suits the old, fawn-eyed one."'
ramayana-7-17-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-20.translation: '"You who have every virtue should not do this. Beauty of the three worlds, do not follow the ways of old age in your youth."'
ramayana-7-17-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-21.translation: '"And who is this you call Vishnu? In valour, austerity, wealth and strength he is not my equal, lady, the one you desire."'
ramayana-7-17-21.meaning: He boasted he was greater than Vishnu.
ramayana-7-17-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-17-22.translation: '"No, no!" the maiden said to the night-roamer. Then the rakshasa reached out and seized her by the hair.'
ramayana-7-17-22.meaning: She refused, and he grabbed her.
ramayana-7-17-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-23.translation: 'Then Vedavati, angry, cut off her hair with her hand, and, prepared a fire, resolved to give up her life, and said:'
ramayana-7-17-23.meaning: She freed herself and prepared to enter a fire.
ramayana-7-17-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-24.translation: '"Ignoble one, now that you have insulted me, I will not keep this life. Before your eyes, rakshasa, I will enter the fire."'
ramayana-7-17-24.meaning: She would not live after being insulted, and entered the fire.
ramayana-7-17-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-25.translation: '"Because I, sinless and as if without protector, have been insulted by you, I will be born again for your destruction."'
ramayana-7-17-25.meaning: She vowed to be reborn to bring about his downfall.
ramayana-7-17-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-26.translation: '"A woman cannot slay you, wicked one; and if I curse you, my austerity would be lost."'
ramayana-7-17-26.meaning: She would not curse him, to keep her merit.
ramayana-7-17-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-27.translation: '"If I have done any good, given gifts or made offerings, by that may I be born, not from a womb, a virtuous daughter of a righteous man."'
ramayana-7-17-27.meaning: She prayed to be reborn as the daughter of a good man.
ramayana-7-17-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-28.translation: 'Having said this, she entered the blazing fire, and a divine shower of flowers fell from heaven on every side.'
ramayana-7-17-28.meaning: She entered the fire, and flowers fell from heaven.
ramayana-7-17-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-29.translation: '"She is the one by whom that enemy, already struck down by her anger, was slain through you, relying on your superhuman, mountain-like valour."'
ramayana-7-17-29.meaning: Agastya told Rama: it was she whose vow led to Ravana's end through you.
ramayana-7-17-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-30.translation: '"Thus this fortunate one is born again among mortals, from a field furrowed by the plough's tip, like a flame from an altar."'
ramayana-7-17-30.meaning: She was reborn from a ploughed field.
ramayana-7-17-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita.

ramayana-7-17-31.translation: '"She was Vedavati in the Krita age; in the Treta age she was born to bring about that rakshasa's end, and because she arose from the furrow (sita), people call her Sita."'
ramayana-7-17-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 17: Ravana insults the devout maiden Vedavati, who enters the fire vowing to return for his downfall; she is reborn as Sita. This links Sita's story to Vedavati's vow.

ramayana-7-18-1.translation: 'When Vedavati had entered the fire, Ravana mounted the Pushpaka and roamed the earth.'
ramayana-7-18-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: Ravana interrupts King Marutta's sacrifice; the gods hide in the forms of birds and animals.

ramayana-7-18-2.translation: 'Then, reaching Ushirabija, the rakshasa saw King Marutta performing a sacrifice with the gods.'
ramayana-7-18-2.meaning: He came upon King Marutta's sacrifice.
ramayana-7-18-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: Ravana interrupts King Marutta's sacrifice; the gods hide in the forms of birds and animals.

ramayana-7-18-3.translation: 'The brahmin sage Samvarta, own brother of Brihaspati and knower of dharma, was conducting it, surrounded by all the brahmins.'
ramayana-7-18-3.meaning: The sage Samvarta led the ritual.
ramayana-7-18-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: Ravana interrupts King Marutta's sacrifice; the gods hide in the forms of birds and animals.

ramayana-7-18-4.translation: 'Seeing that rakshasa, hard to defeat because of his boon, the gods, afraid of his attack, took on various animal forms.'
ramayana-7-18-4.meaning: The gods disguised themselves as animals.
ramayana-7-18-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: Ravana interrupts King Marutta's sacrifice; the gods hide in the forms of birds and animals.

ramayana-7-18-5.translation: 'Indra became a peacock, Dharmaraja a crow, the lord of wealth a lizard, and Varuna a swan.'
ramayana-7-18-5.meaning: Indra became a peacock, Yama a crow, Kubera a lizard and Varuna a swan.
ramayana-7-18-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: Ravana interrupts King Marutta's sacrifice; the gods hide in the forms of birds and animals.

ramayana-7-18-6.translation: 'Approaching that king, Ravana, lord of rakshasas, said, "Give me battle, or say, 'I am defeated.'"'
ramayana-7-18-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-7.translation: 'Then King Marutta said to him, "Who are you?" The rakshasa laughed and said:'
ramayana-7-18-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-8.translation: '"I am pleased, king, by your lack of curiosity, that you do not know me, Ravana, younger brother of the giver of wealth."'
ramayana-7-18-8.meaning: Ravana mocked him for not knowing him.
ramayana-7-18-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-9.translation: '"Who in the three worlds does not know my strength, by which I defeated my brother and took this chariot?"'
ramayana-7-18-9.meaning: He boasted of beating his brother.
ramayana-7-18-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-18-10.translation: 'Then King Marutta said to the rakshasa: "You are fortunate indeed, to have defeated your elder brother in battle!"'
ramayana-7-18-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-11.translation: '"A deed joined with adharma is not praiseworthy, nor approved by the world. Having done a wicked deed, you boast of defeating your brother."'
ramayana-7-18-11.meaning: Marutta said beating one's own brother is nothing to be proud of.
ramayana-7-18-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed. Teaching: victory won by wrong means brings no honour.

ramayana-7-18-12.translation: '"Did you earn your boon in the past by practising dharma alone? I have never heard of anything like what you yourself are saying."'
ramayana-7-18-12.meaning: He questioned how such a person won a boon.
ramayana-7-18-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-13.translation: 'Then the king, taking his bow and arrows, went out angrily to fight, but Samvarta blocked his way.'
ramayana-7-18-13.meaning: Marutta took up his bow, but his priest stopped him.
ramayana-7-18-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-14.translation: 'The great sage said lovingly to Marutta: "If you will listen to me, fighting is not right for you."'
ramayana-7-18-14.meaning: The sage advised him not to fight.
ramayana-7-18-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-15.translation: '"This sacrifice to Maheshvara, left unfinished, would burn your family. How can one who has taken the vow of sacrifice fight? Where is cruelty in one so consecrated?"'
ramayana-7-18-15.meaning: A person in the middle of a sacred vow must not fight.
ramayana-7-18-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed. Teaching: some commitments, once begun, must be honoured above pride.

ramayana-7-18-16.translation: '"And victory in battle is always uncertain, and this rakshasa is hard to beat." At his teacher's word, King Marutta turned back, put down his bow and arrows, and calmly turned again to the sacrifice.'
ramayana-7-18-16.meaning: Marutta obeyed his teacher and returned to the ritual.
ramayana-7-18-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-17.translation: 'Then, thinking him defeated, Shuka proclaimed, "Ravana has won!" and shouted with joy.'
ramayana-7-18-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-18.translation: 'Having harmed the great sages who had come to the sacrifice, he went on across the earth.'
ramayana-7-18-18.meaning: Ravana harmed the sages there and moved on.
ramayana-7-18-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-19.translation: 'When Ravana had gone, the gods with Indra returned to their own forms and spoke to those creatures.'
ramayana-7-18-19.meaning: After Ravana left, the gods took their own forms again.
ramayana-7-18-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-20.translation: 'In joy Indra said to the peacock with its blue tail: "I am pleased with you, knower of dharma, bird, for your help."'
ramayana-7-18-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-21.translation: '"My thousand eyes shall be on your tail. When I send rain you will feel joy, as a sign of my favour."'
ramayana-7-18-21.meaning: Indra gave the peacock its tail of 'eyes' and joy in the rain.
ramayana-7-18-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed. This is a story explaining why peacocks dance in the rain.

ramayana-7-18-22.translation: 'Long ago, king, peacocks' tails were all blue; by the boon of the lord of the gods they all became many-coloured.'
ramayana-7-18-22.meaning: That is why peacock tails are colourful.
ramayana-7-18-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-23.translation: 'Dharmaraja, Rama, said to the crow sitting on the eastern beam: "Bird, I am very pleased with you; hear my words."'
ramayana-7-18-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-24.translation: '"The various diseases with which I afflict other creatures will have no power over you while I am pleased."'
ramayana-7-18-24.meaning: Yama blessed the crow with freedom from disease.
ramayana-7-18-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-25.translation: '"By my boon you shall have no fear of death, bird. You will live until men kill you."'
ramayana-7-18-25.meaning: The crow would not die of natural causes.
ramayana-7-18-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-26.translation: '"And people in my realm who suffer hunger will, with their kin, be satisfied when you are fed."'
ramayana-7-18-26.meaning: Feeding crows would satisfy the hungry departed.
ramayana-7-18-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed. This explains the custom of feeding crows in rites for ancestors.

ramayana-7-18-27.translation: 'Varuna said to the swan that roams the waters of the Ganga: "Hear my words of favour, lord of birds."'
ramayana-7-18-27.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-28.translation: '"Your colour will be lovely and gentle, like the moon's disc, bright as white foam."'
ramayana-7-18-28.meaning: He gave the swan its white colour.
ramayana-7-18-28.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-29.translation: '"Coming to my body, the water, you will always be beautiful and will find unequalled joy; this is the sign of my favour."'
ramayana-7-18-29.meaning: The swan would always be happy in the water.
ramayana-7-18-29.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-30.translation: 'Long ago, Rama, swans were not all white; their wings had dark tips and their breasts were the colour of fresh grass.'
ramayana-7-18-30.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-31.translation: 'Then Vaishravana said to the lizard on the mountain: "I give you a golden colour; I am pleased with you."'
ramayana-7-18-31.meaning: Kubera gave the lizard a golden colour.
ramayana-7-18-31.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-32.translation: '"Your head will always be rich and unfading. This golden colour shall be yours by my favour."'
ramayana-7-18-32.meaning: The lizard's head would shine golden.
ramayana-7-18-32.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-18-33.translation: 'Having given these boons to them at that sacrificial festival, the gods, when it was over, returned with the king to their homes.'
ramayana-7-18-33.meaning: After the sacrifice, the gods went home.
ramayana-7-18-33.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 18: King Marutta, stopped by his priest from fighting during a sacred rite, lets Ravana pass; the gods then bless the creatures whose forms they had borrowed.

ramayana-7-19-1.translation: 'Having overcome Marutta, ten-faced Ravana, lord of rakshasas, went on to the cities of kings, eager for battle.'
ramayana-7-19-1.meaning: Ravana went on to challenge other kings.
ramayana-7-19-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-2.translation: 'Approaching the great kings, equal to Indra and Varuna, the rakshasa lord said, "Give me battle!"'
ramayana-7-19-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-3.translation: '"Or say, 'We are defeated.' This is my resolve. Otherwise you will find no escape."'
ramayana-7-19-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-19-4.translation: 'Then many wise kings firm in dharma, knowing the power of their enemy's boon, said, "We are defeated."'
ramayana-7-19-4.meaning: Many kings wisely chose not to fight.
ramayana-7-19-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-5.translation: 'Dushyanta, Suratha, Gadhi, Gaya and King Pururavas: all these kings said, dear one, "We are defeated."'
ramayana-7-19-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-6.translation: 'Then Ravana, lord of rakshasas, came to Ayodhya, well guarded by Anaranya as Amaravati is by Indra.'
ramayana-7-19-6.meaning: Then he came to Ayodhya, ruled by King Anaranya, Rama's ancestor.
ramayana-7-19-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-7.translation: 'Approaching the king he said, "Give me battle, or say 'I am defeated'. This is my command."'
ramayana-7-19-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-8.translation: 'Anaranya, very angry, said to the rakshasa lord: "I give you single combat, lord of rakshasas."'
ramayana-7-19-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-9.translation: 'Then the king's great army, prepared after hearing the news beforehand, marched out, intent on destroying the rakshasa.'
ramayana-7-19-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-10.translation: 'Many thousands of elephants and ten thousand horses, with foot-soldiers and chariots, covered the earth as they came out in a moment.'
ramayana-7-19-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-11.translation: 'Meeting Ravana's army, that king's army perished, king, like an offering poured into fire.'
ramayana-7-19-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-19-12.translation: 'The king saw his great army destroyed, like water of five rivers reaching the great ocean.'
ramayana-7-19-12.meaning: The king saw his army lost.
ramayana-7-19-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-19-13.translation: 'Then the king, faint with anger, drawing his bow like Indra's, himself went up to Ravana.'
ramayana-7-19-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-14.translation: 'Then the joy of the Ikshvaku line shot eight hundred arrows at the head of the rakshasa king.'
ramayana-7-19-14.meaning: He fired many arrows at Ravana.
ramayana-7-19-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-19-15.translation: 'His arrows, falling, did no harm anywhere, like streams of rain from clouds on a mountain top.'
ramayana-7-19-15.meaning: The arrows could not hurt Ravana.
ramayana-7-19-15.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-16.translation: 'Then the angry rakshasa king struck the king on the head with his palm, and he fell from his chariot.'
ramayana-7-19-16.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-19-17.translation: 'The king fell to the ground, limbs shaking and trembling, like a great sal tree in a forest struck by lightning.'
ramayana-7-19-17.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. Battle scenes are told plainly in the epic; the app keeps them brief.

ramayana-7-19-18.translation: 'The rakshasa laughed and said to the Ikshvaku king: "What have you gained by fighting me?"'
ramayana-7-19-18.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-19.translation: '"No one in the three worlds can face me in single combat, king. I suppose, heedless in your pleasures, you had not heard of my strength."'
ramayana-7-19-19.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-19-20.translation: 'As he spoke, the king, his life ebbing, said: "What can be done here? Time cannot be overcome."'
ramayana-7-19-20.meaning: The dying king spoke calmly about fate.
ramayana-7-19-20.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-21.translation: '"I was not defeated by you, rakshasa, you who praise yourself. I have been brought down here by Time; you are only its instrument."'
ramayana-7-19-21.meaning: He said Time, not Ravana, had defeated him.
ramayana-7-19-21.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. Teaching: the proud take credit for what is really the working of time and fate.

ramayana-7-19-22.translation: '"But what can I do now, as my life ends? Because the Ikshvakus have been insulted, I will say these words, rakshasa."'
ramayana-7-19-22.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-23.translation: '"If I have given, if I have made offerings, if I have done good and practised austerity, if I have protected my people well, then may my words come true."'
ramayana-7-19-23.meaning: By the power of his good life, he spoke a solemn truth.
ramayana-7-19-23.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-24.translation: '"In this family of the great Ikshvakus a king of supreme splendour will be born who will take your life."'
ramayana-7-19-24.meaning: A king of his line, Rama, would end Ravana's life.
ramayana-7-19-24.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life. This prophecy is fulfilled by Rama.

ramayana-7-19-25.translation: 'Then the gods' drum sounded, loud as a thunder-cloud, and when that curse was spoken a shower of flowers fell from the sky.'
ramayana-7-19-25.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-19-26.translation: 'Then the king, great king, went to heaven; and when he had gone to heaven, Rama, the rakshasa turned away.'
ramayana-7-19-26.meaning: Anaranya went to heaven, and Ravana left.
ramayana-7-19-26.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 19: Many kings yield to Ravana; King Anaranya of Ayodhya fights him and, falling, foretells that a king of his line will end Ravana's life.

ramayana-7-20-1.translation: 'Then, terrifying mortals on earth, the rakshasa lord met Narada, best of sages, in a cloud.'
ramayana-7-20-1.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-2.translation: 'Radiant Narada, divine sage of boundless splendour, standing on a cloud, spoke to Ravana in the Pushpaka.'
ramayana-7-20-2.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-3.translation: '"Lord of rakshasas, gentle son of Vishravas, stop. I am pleased with you, well-born one, and with your mighty deeds."'
ramayana-7-20-3.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-4.translation: '"I have been greatly pleased by Vishnu's slaying of daityas, by Garuda's defeat of serpents, and by your crushing in battle."'
ramayana-7-20-4.meaning: He compared Ravana to great heroes.
ramayana-7-20-4.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-5.translation: '"I will tell you something, if you will listen; and having heard it, bull among rakshasas, you should act on it."'
ramayana-7-20-5.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-6.translation: '"Why do you harm this world, you who cannot be slain by the gods? This world is already slain, since it is under the power of death."'
ramayana-7-20-6.meaning: Why trouble mortals? They are already ruled by death.
ramayana-7-20-6.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-7.translation: '"Look, mighty-armed lord of rakshasas, at this human world, so varied, whose course no one knows."'
ramayana-7-20-7.meaning: Look at the human world, full of uncertainty.
ramayana-7-20-7.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-8.translation: '"Here some enjoy music and dance in joy; others weep in pain, tears streaming down their faces."'
ramayana-7-20-8.meaning: Some people celebrate while others weep.
ramayana-7-20-8.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-9.translation: '"Ruined by delusion through love for mother, father, children, wife and kin, these people do not see their own suffering."'
ramayana-7-20-9.meaning: People are so caught up in attachments that they miss their own suffering.
ramayana-7-20-9.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death. Teaching: attachment can blind us to life's deeper truths.

ramayana-7-20-10.translation: '"So why trouble the world, already undone by delusion? The mortal world is already conquered by you, gentle one, without doubt."'
ramayana-7-20-10.meaning: Mortals are no challenge; leave them be.
ramayana-7-20-10.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-11.translation: 'Thus addressed, the lord of Lanka, blazing with power, laughed, bowed to Narada and said:'
ramayana-7-20-11.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-12.translation: '"Great sage, you who wander among gods and gandharvas and love a fight, I am about to go to the underworld seeking victory."'
ramayana-7-20-12.meaning: Ravana said he planned to conquer the underworld.
ramayana-7-20-12.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.

ramayana-7-20-13.translation: '"Then, having conquered the three worlds and brought the nagas and gods under my control, I will churn the ocean for the nectar."'
ramayana-7-20-13.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death. This is the rakshasas' boast; the story shows where such pride leads.

ramayana-7-20-14.translation: 'Then the holy sage Narada said to Dashagriva: "Where are you going now by this road?"'
ramayana-7-20-14.meaning: Narada asked where this road led.
ramayana-7-20-14.explanation: Uttara Kanda, chapter 20: The sage Narada tells Ravana that mortals are already ruled by death, and Ravana sets out to conquer Yama, lord of death.
